title: Solar Particle Event (Coronal Mass Ejection)
description: Space weather sensors detect an incoming proton flux spike from an X-class solar flare. Unshielded surface activity risks severe acute radiation exposure and electronics upsets.
scientific_explanation: Solar Particle Events (SPEs) accelerate protons to relativistic speeds. Without Earth's magnetosphere, astronauts must retreat behind high-mass or hydrogen-rich shielding (water walls or regolith berms) until flux subsides.

decision_options.label: Order all crew into the Radiation Shelter & power down non-essential surface ops
decision_options.tradeoff: Minimizes radiation dose and protects crew health, but consumes 18 kWh emergency shelter power and pauses science production today.

decision_options.label: Reroute water reserves into habitat water-wall bladders & reduce EVA
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 20 L of water for temporary thermal/radiation buffering and 10 kWh pump energy with moderate radiation protection.

decision_options.label: Continue normal surface operations to preserve battery & schedule
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves electrical energy today, but exposes astronauts to dangerous acute solar proton radiation and damages unshielded electronics.

title: Regional Martian Dust Storm Front
description: High-altitude iron-oxide dust clouds are sweeping across the crater basin, reducing atmospheric optical depth (tau) and coating photovoltaic panels.
scientific_explanation: Martian dust storms can obscure 60–90% of direct sunlight for days while fine electrostatically charged dust settles on solar panels and thermal radiators.

decision_options.label: Deploy electrostatic dust-repulsion sweeps & throttle non-critical loads
decision_options.tradeoff: Spends 15 kWh battery reserves to keep solar panels clean, preserving infrastructure condition.

decision_options.label: Send crew in pressurized suits for manual array brushing after peak winds
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 3.5 kg extra oxygen and 10 L suit cooling water, restoring full solar output.

decision_options.label: Ride out the storm on battery reserves without exterior intervention
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves oxygen and water, but dust accumulation reduces energy by 35 kWh and abrades exterior seals.

title: Photovoltaic Wing Micro-Meteoroid & Dust Fault
description: A primary solar array bus reports a voltage drop caused by micro-meteoroid pitting and abrasive regolith accumulation on the gimbal joint.
scientific_explanation: On airless or thin-atmosphere bodies, micrometeoroids hit at hypervelocity (10–70 km/s), requiring modular bypass diodes and robotic array servicing.

decision_options.label: Perform immediate EVA module bypass & gimbal lubrication
decision_options.tradeoff: Consumes 2.5 kg O2 and 12 kWh workshop power to fully restore the solar array.

decision_options.label: Isolate the damaged solar string remotely from Mission Control
decision_options.tradeoff: Zero crew risk, but permanently drops today's net energy by 22 kWh until next overhaul.

title: Battery Cell Thermal Imbalance Alert
description: Battery Storage telemetry flags an over-temperature cell bank during peak discharge cycling.
scientific_explanation: Space-rated lithium-ion battery banks require active liquid cooling loops and cell-balancing electronics to prevent thermal runaway in vacuum environments.

decision_options.label: Flush cooling loop with reserve water & rebalance cells
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 18 L of water and 10 kWh energy to prevent battery degradation.

decision_options.label: Disconnect the overheating battery bank immediately
decision_options.tradeoff: Protects the base from fire risk without using water, but loses 30 kWh stored energy.

title: Water Processor Multifiltration Bed Saturation
description: Conductivity sensors in the Water Recycler indicate organic contaminant breakthrough in the primary filtration bed.
scientific_explanation: NASA's Water Processor Assembly relies on multifiltration beds and a high-temperature catalytic reactor. Saturated filters must be swapped or thermally regenerated to keep water potable.

decision_options.label: Run high-temperature catalytic regeneration & replace filter cartridge
decision_options.tradeoff: Requires 20 kWh electrical energy, preserving full water purity and recovering 15 L.

decision_options.label: Bypass recycler for 24h and draw from potable emergency water tanks
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves electricity during low-power periods, but loses 28 L of unrecycled wastewater.

title: OGA Electrolysis Cell Stack Pressure Fault
description: Deionized water feed sensors in the Oxygen Generator Assembly report bubble lock in the rotary separator.
scientific_explanation: In reduced gravity, separating oxygen and hydrogen gas bubbles from liquid water requires precision rotary separators; faults require purge cycles and reserve O2 tanks.

decision_options.label: Execute high-power nitrogen purge and rebuild electrolysis membrane
decision_options.tradeoff: Consumes 22 kWh energy and 10 L ultra-pure water, restoring +4.0 kg O2 output.

decision_options.label: Crack emergency high-pressure O2 tanks while running at 50% capacity
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves electrical energy today, but net oxygen drops by 5.5 kg.

title: Hydroponic Nutrient Pump & Root Hypoxia Alert
description: Dissolved oxygen levels in the greenhouse nutrient solution dropped overnight, threatening the dwarf wheat and lettuce harvest.
scientific_explanation: In low gravity, water forms thick boundary layers around plant roots, starving them of oxygen unless active aeration and nutrient circulation are maintained.

decision_options.label: Flush nutrient loop with fresh oxygenated water & boost LED spectrum
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 22 L of water and 14 kWh energy to save the harvest (+4.5 kg food).

decision_options.label: Harvest early and sanitize hydroponic trays to conserve water
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves water and power, but yields 6.0 kg less food.

title: Secondary Coolant & Potable Water Line Leak
description: Acoustic sensors detect a pressure drop in the inter-module water transfer umbilical caused by thermal expansion fatigue.
scientific_explanation: Extreme day-night temperature swings on the Moon and Mars cause metal and polymer joints to expand and contract repeatedly, requiring rapid isolation valves.

decision_options.label: Dispatch robotic repair arm & sinter replacement polymer seal
decision_options.tradeoff: Consumes 16 kWh energy and limits water loss to 8 L.

decision_options.label: Close manual bulkhead valves and vent the affected line section
decision_options.tradeoff: Zero energy cost, but vents 32 L of potable water into vacuum.

title: Ka-Band High-Gain Antenna Tracking Drift
description: Atmospheric charging and thermal distortion have misaligned the Deep Space Network transponder dish.
scientific_explanation: High-frequency Ka-band links offer high data rates for NASA science return but require sub-degree pointing accuracy.

decision_options.label: Run high-power calibration sweep and transmit buffered science telemetry
decision_options.tradeoff: Costs 12 kWh energy and awards +8 Planetary Science Points.

decision_options.label: Switch to low-rate UHF backup beacon until next scheduled pass
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves electrical energy, but delays science transmission (-4 Science Points).

title: External Thermal Radiator Dust Blanket
description: Fine electrostatic dust on the habitat's ammonia heat-rejection radiators is reducing heat dissipation efficiency.
scientific_explanation: In a vacuum or thin atmosphere, heat cannot be convected away by air; spacecraft must radiate heat into space via clean high-emissivity radiator panels.

decision_options.label: Activate sublimator water-evaporative cooling & robotic radiator brush
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 15 L water and 10 kWh energy to cool systems and protect equipment.

decision_options.label: Throttle life-support and laboratory electronics to reduce waste heat
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves water, but reduces energy by 18 kWh and crew comfort (-3% health).

title: Airlock Dust Seal & Bearing Abrasion Warning
description: After repeated surface EVAs, razor-sharp regolith grains have scored the primary airlock pressure gasket.
scientific_explanation: Apollo astronauts found that unweathered lunar dust clung electrostatically to suits and caused slow airlock pressure leaks until seals were cleaned and replaced.

decision_options.label: Fabricate new elastomer gasket in Maintenance Workshop & vacuum airlock
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 14 kWh energy to stop the micro-leak and boost infrastructure health (+6%).

decision_options.label: Top up cabin pressure from O2 tanks and defer overhaul
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves workshop power, but loses 4.0 kg oxygen and degrades seal condition (-5%).

title: LiOH & Trace Contaminant Filter Depletion
description: Cabin air quality monitors show rising trace volatile organic compounds and CO2 scrubber cartridge wear.
scientific_explanation: Closed habitats require regenerable amine or metal-oxide CO2 scrubbers and activated charcoal beds to prevent CO2 buildup (hypercapnia).

decision_options.label: Thermally bake and regenerate amine scrubber beds using base power
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 18 kWh energy to fully restore cabin air quality and +2 kg O2 recovery.

decision_options.label: Vent stale cabin air fraction and replenish from oxygen reserves
decision_options.tradeoff: Saves electricity, but costs 4.5 kg oxygen and slight crew fatigue (-3% health).

title: Pressurized ISRU Rover Wheel Actuator Jam
description: During an ice-mining sortie, compacted regolith jammed the rover's front-right drive actuator 1.8 km from base.
scientific_explanation: Surface rovers operate in extreme cold and abrasive dust; modular wheel actuators and winch recovery modes are essential for safe crew return.

decision_options.label: Send rescue EVA team with portable battery pack to free the rover & haul ice
decision_options.tradeoff: Costs 15 kWh energy and 2.5 kg O2, but recovers the rover and +25 L extracted water.

decision_options.label: Jettison the ice payload trailer and limp the rover back on 3-wheel drive
decision_options.tradeoff: Protects crew O2 and battery power, but forfeits today's water haul and damages rover (-4% condition).

title: Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) Flux Surge
description: Heliospheric modulation shifts have increased high-energy heavy-ion (HZE) cosmic ray background readings across the sector.
scientific_explanation: Galactic Cosmic Rays originate outside the solar system and consist of energetic protons and heavy atomic nuclei that penetrate thin aluminum hulls easily.

decision_options.label: Enforce strict indoor duty shifts & administer antioxidant medical countermeasures
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses 3.0 kg medical/food supplements and 8 kWh power, keeping crew health high (+2%) and dose low.

decision_options.label: Maintain standard EVA schedule to advance science objectives
decision_options.tradeoff: Gains +6 Science Points, but increases cumulative radiation dose (+2.4 mSv) and lowers health (-5%).

title: Subsurface Hydrated Mineral & Water-Ice Lens Discovery
description: Ground-penetrating radar on the rover has located a high-purity subsurface ice lens and volatile-rich core sample near the outpost perimeter!
scientific_explanation: Neutron spectrometers (such as NASA's LRO LEND and Mars Odyssey) have confirmed rich subsurface water ice deposits at the lunar poles and Martian mid-to-high latitudes.

decision_options.label: Deploy thermal extraction drills to harvest and purify water & oxygen
decision_options.tradeoff: Invests 20 kWh electrical energy to extract +45 L of water and +5 kg of oxygen!

decision_options.label: Extract pristine geological core samples for the Research Lab
decision_options.tradeoff: Uses only 6 kWh energy, yielding +15 L water and +14 Planetary Science Points.
